The Seed Script

A plain Node script, run through Prisma's CLI, that fills a fresh database with realistic dev data.

Laravel's seeders are classes run through Artisan; Prisma's equivalent is refreshingly plain — just a Node script that imports the Prisma Client (next-but-one topic) and calls it like any other code would. Figure 2.11 is an excerpt of it.

// Figure 2.11: seeding users (prisma/seed.js, excerpt)
import prisma from '../src/config/db.js';

async function main() {
  const customer1 = await prisma.user.create({
    data: {
      name: 'Casey Customer',
      email: 'casey@example.com',
      password: 'placeholder-not-hashed',
      role: 'customer',
    },
  });

  // ...tags, tickets, comments, watchers, a notification — each referencing
  // the ids created above.
}

main().finally(() => prisma.$disconnect());

Nothing here is Prisma-specific syntax to memorise — it's async/await calling ordinary functions, the same shape as every service function in this project. The password value is a plain placeholder string, not a real hash — Week 4 introduces bcrypt and hashes passwords for real; seed data doesn't need to pretend otherwise yet.

Running it goes through Prisma's own CLI rather than plain node:

npx prisma db seed

which is possible only because of the "prisma": { "seed": "node prisma/seed.js" } line back in Figure 2.3 — that's the config db seed actually reads to know which file to run.
